reviews.text: So Grateful. Like most people who have that deep-down feeling that they drink too much, I did my best to avoid really thinking about it too hard for a long time a decade or so. Eventually the concern set in, but the thought of giving up alcohol sounded both unappealing and, frankly, impossible. I downloaded Sunnyside because I liked the idea of moderation over abstinence, and thought it would be a useful tool to help me get there. Once I started setting my weekly goals (starting with a GENEROUS number, since I didn’t want to feel like a failure off the bat) and tracking nightly drinks, it quickly became apparent that I was drinking significantly more than I even realized. Did the app help me reduce by being more mindful? I’m not really sure, maybe. But the most useful function, for me, was just the tracking and accountability. Week after week, I exceeded the number of drinks I planned, and that was with me putting forth a real effort to moderate…which wasn’t going very well but WAS taking up a whole lot of mental energy. After about 3 months, I had all the information I really needed: it was clear that any efforts I made to moderate were incredibly challenging (and really took the care-free nature of drinking out of it), and even still I was unable to meet my (relatively unambitious) goals. More than anything else in my life (including two DUIs and nearly having to do court-mandated treatment, all the while insisting and genuinely convinced I didn’t have a problem), this app was the evidence *I* needed to know what I’d been trying to avoid for so long: I really did have a problem, and moderation just wasn’t going to be a winning strategy. And for the first time, I actually wanted to quit. Armed with the acceptance that something needed to change, I can’t recommend Annie Grace’s “This Naked Mind” book enough for making that first step into the world of sobriety…and I can happily say I haven’t had a drink in over 14 months, and feel committed to keep it that way. Picturing the shame I felt while reviewing my old metrics on Sunnyside keeps me objective about the whole thing. I know exactly where I’ve been, instead of thinking maybe it wasn’t as bad as it was, or that this time could be different. I gave myself months of tracking to demonstrate either of those things, and the data spoke for itself. At the end of the day, that was the best choice for me. reviews.text: Finally, something that works for me!. I want this to be about Sunnyside and not me, but a little bit of info about me and my drinking gives perspective as to why Sunnyside is such a good fit for me. I am 73 and have been drinking since I was 15, except for 6 years between 2009 and 2014 when I stopped completely because of laryngeal cancer caused by GERD. I gave up “hard liquor” in 2009 because there are no lines on the bottle. Beer is my choice, which makes Sunnyside work for me because it is easy to count drinks. Two of my three daughters are alcoholics, one is in recovery, the other is in denial. I went to an “open” AA meeting with the one in recovery, but I realized AA is not for me. It works GREAT for me, IF I follow the suggested program. To drink with mindfulness, I must track my drinks in real time. A couple of times I did not do that, and I went over my goals. Building in at least 1 dry day brings a completely different perspective to the whole drinking experience, even though for me, that dry day is challenging. The coaching BOT is great. The real live coaches are wonderful. The Community element really encourages me with my own drinking, and with sending love to those who are themselves struggling. I look at SS as a “Third Rail” between drinking “devil may care” and total abstinence. I hope to look back a year from now and see that I made real progress since joining SS. I highly recommend Sunnyside!

Sorry to see you go! Is there something we could have done differently to make the experience more valuable for you? If you ever want to jump back in, you know where to find us. Simply reply START to reactivate your account.”

My response then, and my review now, is this: Yes, you can give people the option to opt out of your spam text inviting them to stupid groups that they don't want to participate in instead of just canceling their accounts unilaterally.

I think you can still use the tracking part of the app, but I actually liked getting text messages that would remind me to track it. I just didn’t want all the extra frequent communications about things I don’t care about.

Mindful drinking. This app is helping me think about drinking instead of just pouring a glass whenever I have the impulse, which I’ve come to realize I was doing before starting Sunnyside about a month ago. 

I’m not trying to stop drinking, just reduce it quite a bit, and pay attention to when I do drink. On Sunday night, I make my plan for the week, and now I’m up to 5 dry days a week (when I used to drink every day), only drinking Friday and Saturday. I’m sleeping so much better and saving money!

The app makes it easy with text reminders, encouragement, and celebrations. There are a lot of interactive features that I haven’t even started using yet. I’m so glad I discovered Sunnyside.
